title: Constant coefficients have unit stalk trace
statement:
Use the commutative finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ ($n\geq1$) and
algebraically closed base field $k$ of characteristic $p\neq\ell$ from
[def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Let $X$ be a separated
finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and let $h:X\to X$ be a $k$-endomorphism. Put $K=A_X$ in degree zero, the constant complex on the
small pro-etale site. Let
$$u:Lh^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}K$$
be the canonical unit comparison induced by the constant coefficient identification in
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. For every geometric point
$\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ fixed by $h$, meaning $h\circ\bar x=\bar x$, use the canonical stalk identification
$(Lh^*K)_{\bar x}\simeq K_{\bar x}$ and write $u_{\bar x}:K_{\bar x}\to K_{\bar x}$ for the
induced endomorphism. Then
$$\operatorname{tr}_A(u_{\bar x}\mid K_{\bar x})=1$$
in the sense of [def-trf-categorical-trace]. Moreover, $K$ is site-perfect in the sense of
[def-weil-site-perfect-complex].

proof.text: Use the identity covering $\{X\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}X\}$. On it $K$ is represented by the complex with only $P^0=A_X$ nonzero. Its degree-zero term is a direct summand of the one-fold sum $A_X$ by the two identity maps; the zero terms are direct summands of zero-fold sums. This is exactly a bounded finite-projective representative in [def-weil-site-perfect-complex], proving site-perfectness.

Apply [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] with $u=h$ and $\Lambda=A$; this is permitted because $A=A_{E,n}$ is finite discrete. It supplies the canonical isomorphism $c_A^h:h^{-1}A_X\to A_X$. Its adjoint sends the constant section $a$ to the same constant section $a$ after base change. By the finite-level termwise model in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], $Lh^*(A_X[0])$ is $h^{-1}A_X[0]$ with its coefficient action transported through $c_A^h$. Thus $c_A^h[0]$ is the specified $u$. In the extension-of-scalars presentation the same map is $m\otimes b\mapsto c_A^h(m)b$, with inverse $b\mapsto1\otimes b$; balancing gives both inverse identities.

Fix $\bar x$ with $h\bar x=\bar x$. By [lem-weil-proetale-constant-sheaf-stalk] with $M=A$, the constant-germ map $\gamma_{\bar x}:A\to(A_X)_{\bar x}$ is an isomorphism. Write $d_{\bar x}=(c_A^h)_{\bar x}$. In the inverse-image colimit of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] at $U=X$, take $V=X$ (the final target-site object) and the unique map $\phi:X\to h^*X\simeq X$. Send the global constant section $a$ through this coprojection and sheafification, then take its germ at $(X,\bar x)$ using [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]; call the resulting map $t_{\bar x}:A\to(h^{-1}A_X)_{\bar x}$. The adjunction defining $c_A^h$ and its constant-section formula in [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] give $d_{\bar x}t_{\bar x}(a)=\gamma_{\bar x}(a)$ for every $a$. Since $c_A^h$ is an isomorphism, so is $d_{\bar x}$, hence $t_{\bar x}$ is an isomorphism. The canonical pullback comparison on these constant stalks is $b_{\bar x}=t_{\bar x}\gamma_{\bar x}^{-1}:(A_X)_{h\bar x}\to(h^{-1}A_X)_{\bar x}$: its value on a constant germ is precisely the coprojection just described, and all source germs are constant by the stalk lemma. Thus $u_{\bar x}\gamma_{\bar x}(a)=d_{\bar x}b_{\bar x}\gamma_{\bar x}(a)=\gamma_{\bar x}(a)$ for every $a$. Surjectivity of $\gamma_{\bar x}$ proves that $u_{\bar x}$ is the identity, and identifies the stalk complex with $A[0]$.

Compute the degree-zero chain trace directly from [def-trf-categorical-trace], which is the degree-zero specialization of the source's supertrace calculation. Use the representative $B^0=A$ with representative isomorphism $\alpha=\gamma_{\bar x}[0]$ from step 3, and use the identity splitting $A\to A\to A$, with sole dual-frame pair $e=1$ and $\epsilon(a)=a$. All differentials are zero. Coevaluation sends $1$ to $1\otimes\epsilon$; the stalk identity leaves this unchanged; the Koszul symmetry has sign $(-1)^{0\cdot0}=1$ and sends it to $\epsilon\otimes1$; evaluation returns $\epsilon(1)=1$. The defined scalar identification evaluates this endomorphism of $A[0]$ at $1$, so the trace is $1\in A$. No other degree contributes. Here we used one bounded projective representative and one splitting; by the invariance assertion of [lem-trf-chain-supertrace] (the formulas are invariant under chain homotopy, choice of dual frame, and replacement of the representative and endomorphism by an isomorphic pair in $D(A)$, and agree with the trace of [def-trf-categorical-trace]), this value is $\operatorname{tr}_A(u_{\bar x}\mid K_{\bar x})$ for every admissible choice in that definition. Equivalently, part (c) of that lemma gives $(-1)^0\operatorname{Tr}_A(1\mid A)=\epsilon(1)=1$.

split_report.summary: STATEMENT-DISPUTED (unbound ambient objects): made the finite-coefficient convention, X, h, canonical u and fixed geometric point explicit, retaining the source ambient separated finite-type setting. Expanded the proof into site-perfectness from the identity cover, actual constant-coefficient pullback on sections, its identity action on constant germs, and the direct degree-zero categorical trace composite. Reused the existing canonical coefficient-ring isomorphism and constant pro-etale stalk lemma; no new nodes. The direct rank-one trace calculation needs no general supertrace theorem. The second reading specifies the constant-stalk pullback comparison and the representative isomorphism explicitly, and separates the coefficient/base-field convention from the independent scheme binder.
